Good, I got 4 of 6 searches through. Let me process the results and update my working list.

Key findings from Turn 2:

1. **Cam Pha**: GEM wiki confirms 680 MW total, Phase I was 2×300 MW = 600 MW, completed Sept 2011. The iLotusLand source confirms 600 MW capacity. But GEM says "at least 680-megawatts" with "multiple units, some of which are not currently operating." So there may be older units (80 MW) on top of the 600 MW Phase I. 

Looking more carefully at the GEM page, it mentions the plant was initially conceptualized as 260 MW before the first phase was upgraded to 600 MW with two 300 MW boilers, so the "at least 680" figure likely includes some older decommissioned units. The iLotusLand source confirms exactly 600 MW operating, so I'll go with that.

2. **Vinh Tan 3**: 1,980 MW (3×660 MW supercritical). CLP pulled out Dec 2019, Mitsubishi in Feb 2021, and HSBC withdrew as financial advisor in Jan 2020. The GEM wiki still lists it as "under development" with recent 2024-2025 references mentioning India investing $10 billion and Vingroup exploring $30 billion investments, suggesting new investors may be exploring the project. Status: Shelved, though not officially cancelled and the PDP8 didn't explicitly cancel it.

3. **Long Phu 1**: 1,200 MW (2×600). It was roughly 70% complete when Russian contractor Power Machines withdrew due to US sanctions in Jan 2018, but PVN relaunched the project in Jan 2025 with boiler installation beginning in Apr 2025 and a target completion before 2027. Status: Under construction.

4. **Nam Dinh 1**: Planned as a 1,200 MW coal plant with investors Taekwang and ACWA, though the status remains uncertain.

5. **Quang Ninh 1 & 2**: 4×300 MW totaling 1,200 MW. QN1 came online in May 2009 and June 2010, while QN2 started construction in May 2007 with units completed around 2012-2013. Quang Ninh Thermal Power JSC, majority-owned by EVN, operates both.

6. **Mong Duong 1**: 1,080 MW (2×540) using CFB technology, operated by EVN.

For Mong Duong 2, I found it's a 1,240 MW plant (2×620) developed by AES and POSCO under a BOT arrangement, with Unit 1 coming online in Q1 2015 and Unit 2 in Q3 2015. AES divested their stake in November 2023. I also spotted a reference to Mong Duong 3 as a 1,240 MW project supposedly in final stages, though this information seems outdated or possibly conflated with another project.

For Vung Ang 3, I can confirm it's shelved and not included in PDP8—it was a Samsung/KEPCO joint venture that didn't move forward. I still need to search for details on Bac Lieu LNG, Phu My complex breakdown, Thu Duc and Hiep Phuoc gas plants, Nam Dinh 1, and the O Mon and Son My units. With my remaining token budget, I should move into the final report phase and fill in what I can from existing knowledge.
